ai.title: Improve debug log organization
ai.summary: Refactor logging infrastructure to use `appendFileSync` in dev mode and switch log extensions to `.jsonl`. `cli/src/utils/logger.ts` and `web/src/util/logger.ts` now bypass `pino`'s async transport in development to ensure real-time visibility, addressing Bun compatibility issues. `scripts/dev.sh` reorganizes startup logic and updates log directory paths to `debug/console`. `sdk/package.json` adds a `dev` script mapping to `build`.

eli5.text: When you run the development tools, the behind-the-scenes messages it records while working are now saved in a clearer, more organized way, and they appear faster so you can see what's happening in real time. The startup script that launches the development environment now sorts its record-keeping into a single folder for the console output, and the software development kit gained a shortcut command for building the project during development. If you were watching the logs while the system started up, you would notice the messages showing up without the delay they had before.

ai.title: Add context-pruner integration tests
ai.summary: Added `.agents/__tests__/context-pruner.integration.test.ts` to verify `context-pruner` agent behavior. Tests ensure message history pruning maintains tool-call/tool-result pair integrity for Anthropic API compliance. Covers standard and aggressive pruning scenarios using `claude-haiku-4.5`.

eli5.text: The software now has a new set of checks that verify the conversation-history trimming works without breaking the link between the assistant's tool calls and the tool's responses. These checks run automatically with the other internal tests and do not change what the assistant does today. If you looked at the test folder, you would find a new file containing scenarios that build a large conversation with paired tool messages and confirm that, after trimming, each tool call still matches its corresponding result. The addition is in place for the team running the tests; no user-facing behavior changes yet.

ai.title: Fix .agents test logic to fail correctly
ai.summary: CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` updated to correctly propagate test failures for the `.agents` package. Previous logic used `|| echo` which masked non-zero exit codes from `bun test`. New logic checks for test files explicitly and runs them without suppressing errors, ensuring CI fails when tests fail.

eli5.text: When the continuous integration system ran tests for the internal tooling package, it used to swallow any test failures and report success even when tests broke. Now the system properly runs the tests and fails the build when something goes wrong. You, as someone running code through this pipeline, would now see genuine test failures instead of false passes; behind the scenes, the workflow stopped suppressing errors from the test runner and only prints a fallback message when no test files exist.

ai.title: spawnagents tool schema emphasis and examples
ai.summary: Updated `spawn-agents.ts` to mandate checking required fields in agent params schemas. Added explicit warning that fields like `command` for `commander` or `searchQueries` for `code-searcher` are required. Replaced generic example with concrete `commander` and `code-searcher` invocations demonstrating correct nested `params` usage.

eli5.text: The instructions that tell the system how to start helper programs now spell out, in one place, which settings are mandatory before a program runs. If you ask it to launch a search helper, you must already provide search terms; if you launch a command runner, you must already provide the command. The example shown is now a real search and a real command instead of a made-up task. This is live today: anyone reading those instructions will see the required fields called out and a working example to follow.

ai.title: Fix duplicate text in subagent streaming view
ai.summary: Removed redundant text buffering and flushing logic in `processStreamWithTools` and `processStream` to prevent duplicate text rendering in subagent streaming views. The `onResponseChunk` callback in `tool-stream-parser.ts` was stripped of its internal buffer management, delegating text handling directly to the consumer. In `tools/stream-parser.ts`, `assistantMessages` are now populated directly from the main text chunk stream, eliminating the previous double-push caused by the parser's flush mechanism. This change affects the Agent Runtime SDK, specifically `packages/agent-runtime/src/tool-stream-parser.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant works through a problem step by step and shows you its reasoning as it goes, you may have seen some words appear twice in a row. That happened because the tool was saving up pieces of text and then replaying them, instead of just passing each piece along once. The extra saving and replaying has been removed, so the text you watch stream in now appears only once, matching what the assistant actually says.

ai.title: Remove flaky message count assertion in context-pruner integration
ai.summary: Removed the `expect(finalMessages.length).toBeLessThan(...)` assertion from `.agents/__tests__/context-pruner.integration.test.ts`. The check was flaky because agent runs add messages and context pruning may replace messages with placeholders rather than removing them. The test now relies on verifying that tool-call/tool-result pairs remain intact.

eli5.text: The system stopped checking how many messages are left after the assistant runs, because the count kept jumping around for two reasons: each run adds its own messages, and trimming context sometimes swaps big chunks of text for short placeholders instead of deleting them outright. If you watched a run now, you would no longer see the test fail just because the inbox got a little longer or the trimmer left placeholder notes behind; the test instead focuses on confirming the assistant's tool calls and their replies still match up correctly.

ai.title: CLI suggestion menus now support mouse click and hover
ai.summary: Suggestion menus in cli/src/components/suggestion-menu.tsx now accept onItemClick handlers and render as interactive Button components. Hover state is tracked locally, with visual highlighting applied only after the first mouseover event to prevent accidental selection during initial render. Click handlers in cli/src/chat.tsx update the input value and cursor position directly, bypassing the need for keyboard navigation to confirm selections. This change affects both slash command and mention/file suggestion surfaces in the CLI.

eli5.text: When you are typing a command in the CLI and a menu of suggestions pops up (like slash commands /... or mentions @...), you can now click an item with your mouse instead of having to arrow down and hit Enter. Hovering over a suggestion will also briefly highlight it, but this highlighting only kicks in after youve first moved your mouse over the menu, so the selection doesnt accidentally jump around while the list is first appearing. Both the main chat slash/mention suggestions and the file suggestion surfaces work this way, and clicking one drops the typed shortcut straight into your input and places your cursor ready to keep typing.

ai.title: Exit image mode on paste or path
ai.summary: addPendingImageFromFile now calls exitImageModeIfActive on success, resetting inputMode from 'image' to 'default'. Fixes stuck image mode when adding images via paste or file path. Scope limited to cli/src/utils/add-pending-image.ts. Logic checks useChatStore state and triggers setInputMode only if currently in image mode.

eli5.text: If you paste an image or type a path to an image into the command-line assistant and it successfully adds the picture, the assistant will now automatically switch off its dedicated image-insert mode and return you to normal text input. Previously, after adding an image this way, the interface could stay locked in image mode, leaving you unable to resume regular conversation without manually escaping. This only affects the command-line version of the assistant and happens every time an image is added through these methods.

ai.title: SDK adds e2e test suite and runnable examples
ai.summary: New `sdk/e2e` directory introduces structured end-to-end testing infrastructure and runnable examples for the Codebuff SDK. Tests cover streaming, workflows, custom agents, and specific features like `knowledgeFiles` and `maxAgentSteps`, while examples demonstrate common patterns such as code review and refactoring. Scripts require `CODEBUFF_API_KEY` and are executed via `bun run`. Documentation in `sdk/e2e/README.md` details directory structure and test commands (`test:e2e`, `test:integration`, `test:unit:e2e`).

eli5.text: The SDK now ships with a complete set of automated tests and ready-to-run example scripts that developers can use to verify their integrations and see common workflows in action. When you open the SDK package youll find a dedicated testing area organized by category-streaming, multi-step workflows, custom agents, and specific features like file handling and step limits-along with step-by-step instructions for running each group. The examples show how to perform tasks such as reviewing code, generating commit messages, and explaining code in plain language, all runnable with a single command after adding an API key. This makes it easier to catch problems and learn patterns without writing tests or scripts from scratch.
